messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High KV_CACHE_EVICT_RATE on prod cluster 'us-west-2' (evictions spiked). PagerDuty triggered. thread=1889012345
Alex P: seeing tons of 500s from the routing layer, correlates with cache miss storms. Starting triage.
Alex P: quick snapshot: eviction_count ~ 4.2k/min, kv_hit_rate down to ~58% from baseline ~92%. Latency p50 up ~60ms, p95 up ~450ms.
Jordan L: tagging in. any deploys in last 30m?
Alex P: nothing from deploy-bot. ops-bot shows no kube rolling updates. suspect cache compaction/eviction policy or sudden traffic shape change.
Priya S: checking runtime logs now. pulling recent cache evict traces.
Priya S: log snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T21:01:17Z WARN cache: evict key=usr-1234 size=512 B reason=memory_pressure
2026-03-15T21:01:17Z INFO cache: current_entries=980k max_entries=1m
2026-03-15T21:01:18Z WARN cache: evict_batch=1200 latency_ms=8
```
Alex P: looks like a bursty workload caused batch evictions. could be a bad actor or sudden traffic pattern.
Maria K: CS note: two paying customers reported elevated latencies and some request failures ~20:58-21:10 UTC. They are on Dedicated capacity but route through shared cache layer.
Alex P: estimating customer impact: ~2 customers, ~3% of overall requests errored during peak. We'll notify CS after mitigation.
Jordan L: immediate mitigation options: 1) increase max_entries for KV cache (hot patch config), 2) temporarily disable aggressive compaction flags, 3) add local fallback cache in route path. I'd do 1) first.
Priya S: agree. config change is low-risk: bump max_entries from 1_000_000 to 1_400_000 on us-west-2 cache-pool. drafting command.
Alex P: executing now (will run on subset canaries then scale):
```
# increase kv cache size on config service
curl -X PATCH 'https://config.prod.internal/v1/caches/kv-usw2' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"max_entries":1400000}'
```
Alex P: applied to 10% canary group. monitoring.
Priya S: hit rate on canary nodes jumped from 57% -> 85% within 90s. eviction_count dropped ~78%.
Jordan L: rolling to remaining nodes.
ops-bot: deploy:config-update succeeded for group 100% (1889012378)
Alex P: rolling complete. cluster-level hit rate now ~87%, evictions ~400/min. latencies trending down.
Maria K: notified affected customers with status update. they acknowledged and appreciate the quick response.
Alex P: root cause theory: sudden change in request key distribution (many new unique keys), combined with conservative max_entries setting + old eviction threshold. we'll investigate upstream caller patterns.
Jordan L: postmortem action items (immediate):
- create dedicated dashboard for kv hit-rate and eviction bursts (per-pool, per-shard).
- add alert: sustained kv_hit_rate < 70% for 5m -> P1 (to reduce noisy pages for transient blips).
- add alert: eviction_count_rate > 2k/min for 1m -> P1 (burst eviction alarm).
- add alert: eviction_batch_size > 1000 -> P2 (helps pinpoint compaction events).
- add runbook steps for hot-patch max_entries and fallback toggles.
Priya S: note on alert tuning: previous eviction_count threshold was 500/min which created noise and was triggering on short spikes. suggestion: use rate & duration windows (1m & sustained 5m) and incorporate hit-rate as a suppressor.
Alex P: agreed. also add a dashboard panel to show top-10 keys by churn over last 15m (helps spot noisy clients).
Maria K: I'll coordinate customer comms and include mitigation timeline. also ask Customer Success to flag any correlated SDK/agent upgrades from customers.
Jordan L: creating the monitoring tickets now. PromQL snippets for dashboards/alerts: 
```
# kv hit rate
sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[1m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[1m]))
# eviction rate
sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m]))
```
Alex P: pushing PR for alert changes and dashboard additions. linking in ticket SRE-789.
Priya S: post-incident ops: schedule a workload replay to reproduce churn, and run a capacity test raising unique key cardinality.
Alex P: adding notes to incident doc and will prepare a short blameless postmortem.
Jordan L: once PR merges, we should mute the old eviction alert and ensure alert routing goes to oncall-escalation only when both eviction_count and hit_rate conditions meet.
Maria K: customer's timeline for next update: I'll send a follow-up in 2 hours with RCA stub.
Alex P: handing off to Priya S for night coverage and follow-ups. Priya, you're the incident owner for after-hours. please ack.
Priya S: ack. I'll monitor dashboards for the next 6 hours and start the replay job first thing. filing follow-up tasks -> SRE-790 (dashboards), SRE-791 (runbook), SRE-792 (replay). :thumbsup:
Alex P: thanks team. closing page, will mark incident as mitigated.
oncall-bot: Incident 1889012345 status changed -> mitigated (1889012948)
